Most recent status: the complex reached mechanical completion July 2021 and began operations on Jan 20, 2022, and remains operational; the freshest dedicated reporting dates to the 2022 startup, with no major status change since.

ExxonMobil and SABIC announced their final decision on June 13, 2019 to proceed with Gulf Coast Growth Ventures, a ~$10B 50/50 petrochemical complex (1.8M t/yr ethane steam cracker plus two polyethylene units and a monoethylene glycol unit) near Gregory, San Patricio County, Texas (~600 permanent jobs; clears the floor on capital). Most recent status: the complex reached mechanical completion July 2021 and began operations on Jan 20, 2022, and remains operational; the freshest dedicated reporting dates to the 2022 startup, with no major status change since.

Anduril Industries announced Arsenal-1, a ~$1B (≈$910.5M capital) autonomous-systems/defense manufacturing megafactory (5M sq ft, 4,008 direct jobs by 2035) in Pickaway County, Ohio near Rickenbacker Airport, on Jan 16, 2025. Most recent status (JobsOhio, Jul 27, 2026): the first Ohio-built Fury aircraft rolled off the Arsenal-1 production line, with production having begun in March 2026 — the plant is now in production.

The LEGO Group announced a >$1B precision plastic-brick manufacturing plant (1.7M sq ft, 1,760+ direct jobs) at Meadowville Technology Park in Chesterfield County, Virginia on June 15, 2022. Most recent status (LEGO, Oct 1, 2025): structural steel topped out and the site is under construction, with full production now slated for 2027 (delayed from the originally announced second half of 2025); ~500 employees on site ramping toward 900 by end of 2026.

Novo Nordisk announced a $4.1B expansion adding a second fill/finish aseptic pharmaceutical manufacturing facility (1.4M sq ft, ~1,000 new direct jobs) at its Clayton campus in Johnston County, North Carolina on June 24, 2024. Most recent credible status found (project tracker, published July 2024 — no fresher dated update located): preliminary clearing and foundational work under way, with construction to be completed progressively between 2027 and 2029; not yet producing.

Ford and SK Innovation (SK On) announced BlueOval SK Battery Park, a ~$5.8B twin lithium-ion EV battery cell manufacturing complex (~5,000 direct jobs) in Glendale, Hardin County, Kentucky on Sep 27, 2021 (a separate site from the already-collected BlueOval City in Tennessee). Most recent status (WKU Public Radio, Feb 9, 2026): EV battery production began in Aug 2025 but the plant closed in Dec 2025 with ~1,600 layoffs; the Ford–SK On joint venture was dissolved, Ford took sole ownership, and the site is being repurposed under 'Ford Energy' to make grid/data-center battery energy storage, with production slated to restart in late 2027.

Amkor Technology announced in November 2023 a ~$2B outsourced advanced semiconductor packaging and test facility (~2,000 direct jobs, 55 acres) in Peoria, Arizona, to package/test chips for Apple from the nearby TSMC fab. Most recent status (Construction Dive, Oct 10, 2025): Amkor broke ground on Oct 6, 2025 and expanded the project to a ~$7B two-phase campus; the first facility is under construction with completion expected mid-2027 and production beginning in early 2028 — not yet producing.

Stellantis and Samsung SDI (JV StarPlus Energy) announced a ~$2.5B lithium-ion EV battery cell/module gigafactory (first US plant, ~1,400 direct jobs, 23-33 GWh) in Kokomo, Indiana in May 2022. Most recent status (InkFreeNews, Feb 2026): the first plant began production in 2024 and has shifted part of its output to energy-storage cells, while Stellantis is weighing a possible withdrawal and sale of its StarPlus stake amid EV pullback.

VinFast announced on Mar 29, 2022 a greenfield EV assembly plant at the Triangle Innovation Point megasite in Chatham County (Moncure), North Carolina, pledging up to $4B (~$2B phase 1) and 7,500 jobs. Most recent status (NC Newsline, May 21, 2026): the Moncure site has been largely abandoned since end-2024, permits lapsed, and NC filed suit to claw back the land and ~$80M after the state declared VinFast in default.

Cree (now Wolfspeed) announced on Sep 23, 2019 an ~$1B 200mm silicon-carbide device fabrication facility (the Mohawk Valley Fab) at the Marcy Nanocenter in Marcy, Oneida County, New York. Most recent status (Manufacturing Dive, Dec 4, 2025): the fab is actively producing 200mm SiC wafers (~half of Wolfspeed's quarterly revenue) and ramping utilization after Wolfspeed exited Chapter 11 in Sep 2025 and received ~$699M in CHIPS Act tax refunds.

CF Industries, JERA and Mitsui announced on Apr 8, 2025 a final investment decision on the ~$4B Blue Point Complex, a greenfield low-carbon (carbon-capture) ammonia manufacturing plant billed as the world's largest, at the RiverPlex MegaPark in Ascension Parish, Louisiana (~103 direct jobs; clears the floor on capital). Most recent status (Baton Rouge Business Report, Aug 25, 2026): groundbreaking was held in late August 2026 and major construction has begun on a ~4-year buildout, with commercial operations targeted for 2029 (not yet producing).

Eli Lilly announced on Jan 28, 2022 a greenfield >$1B parenteral (injectable) products and devices manufacturing plant with ~600 direct jobs in Concord, Cabarrus County, North Carolina (a distinct facility from Lilly's LEAP Lebanon, IN site; later scaled up to a ~$2B investment). Most recent status (Pharmaceutical Technology project page): the ~1.3M sq ft facility opened and became operational in June 2024 and is producing injectable products (used for GLP-1 drugs).

Wolfspeed announced on Sep 9, 2022 the John Palmour Manufacturing Center, a ~$5B silicon carbide materials facility (200mm wafers, ~1,800 direct jobs) on the Chatham-Siler City Advanced Manufacturing site in Siler City, Chatham County, NC. Most recent status (Wolfspeed Q1 FY2026 earnings, Oct 29, 2025): after a June 30, 2025 Chapter 11 filing and ~91-day exit, the Siler City plant reached production readiness in late FY2025 but is running underutilized.

Redwood Materials announced on Dec 14, 2022 a ~$3.5B battery-materials campus (anode/cathode plus recycling, 1,500 direct jobs) at Camp Hall Commerce Park in Ridgeville, Berkeley County, SC. Most recent status (Redwood release, Nov 6, 2025): the Carolina Campus has begun critical-materials recovery, bringing its first South Carolina operations online.

Novelis announced on May 11, 2022 a ~$2.5B low-carbon aluminum recycling and rolling mill (600 kilotonnes/yr, ~1,000 direct jobs) at the South Alabama Mega Site in Bay Minette, Baldwin County, AL — the first fully integrated aluminum mill built in the U.S. in 40 years. Most recent status (Construction Dive, Aug 28, 2026): cost has grown to ~$5B, construction is wrapping, cold-mill commissioning began March 2026 with full commissioning expected before year-end 2026 (not yet producing).

AstraZeneca announced in July 2025 a ~$3.5B drug-substance/API manufacturing facility at the Rivanna Futures site in Albemarle County, VA (near Charlottesville) as part of its $50B US plan; the investment was raised to ~$4.5B on Oct 9, 2025. Most recent status (Fierce Pharma, Oct 2025): AstraZeneca broke ground and began construction in October 2025, with the plant expected operational in about 4-5 years.

Methanex reached a final investment decision on July 19, 2019 to build Geismar 3, a ~$1.3B, 1.8 million-tonne/yr methanol plant adjacent to its Geismar 1 and 2 units in Ascension Parish (Geismar), Louisiana. Most recent status (Methanex release, May 1, 2025): after construction was paused in 2020 and restarted in Oct 2021, G3 reached production in mid-2024 and, following an unplanned outage in Feb 2025, successfully restarted in May 2025 and is operating/producing methanol.

Maxeon Solar Technologies announced on Aug 10, 2023 a ~$1B (later cited ~$1.9B) 3 GW solar cell and panel manufacturing facility at Mesa del Sol in Albuquerque, New Mexico (~1,800 direct jobs), with production slated for 2025. Most-recent status (pv magazine USA, Apr 6, 2026): Maxeon abandoned the Albuquerque lease in Feb 2026 and applied for judicial management in Singapore; the facility was never built.

Gotion Inc. announced on Oct 5, 2022 a ~$2.36B lithium-ion battery component (cathode/anode) manufacturing facility in Green Charter Township near Big Rapids, Michigan (up to 2,350 direct jobs). Most-recent status (Michigan Public, Feb 13, 2026): the project is effectively abandoned after local opposition blocked permits; Michigan declared Gotion in default in late 2025 and is clawing back ~$175M in incentives, with grant-repayment and township litigation ongoing. The plant was never built.

Merck announced and broke ground on Apr 29, 2025 on a ~$1B, 470,000-sq-ft biologics 'Center of Excellence' at Chestnut Run Innovation & Science Park (CRISP) in Wilmington, Delaware (500+ direct jobs), intended to make next-generation biologics/antibody-drug conjugates and to become the future U.S. home for KEYTRUDA. Most-recent status: the facility is under construction following the April 2025 groundbreaking, with the lab component targeted to be operational by 2028 and commercial output by 2030; no milestone more recent than the construction start has been reported.

Tesla announced on Jul 22, 2020 (Q2 earnings call / Travis County incentive vote) Gigafactory Texas, an EV assembly plant in the Del Valle area of Travis County near Austin, Texas, with over $1.1B in initial capital investment and at least 5,000 direct jobs. Most-recent status (TechCrunch, Apr 3, 2026): the factory opened in 2022, has had >$6.3B invested, and remains operational producing Model Y and Cybertruck; year-end 2025 employment was 16,506, down ~22% from 21,191 at end-2024 amid a sales slump.

SkyWater Technology announced on Jul 20, 2022 a ~$1.8B, 600,000-sq-ft greenfield semiconductor R&D and fabrication facility in the Discovery Park District at Purdue University in West Lafayette, Indiana (~750 direct jobs) — clears the floor on capital. Most-recent status (Indianapolis Business Journal, Apr 5, 2024): SkyWater released its option on the land and will not build the facility, citing uncertainty over CHIPS Act funding it ultimately did not receive; the project remains cancelled with no revival reported since.

GlobalWafers (via subsidiary GlobiTech) announced on Jun 27, 2022 a ~$5B greenfield 300mm silicon wafer manufacturing plant (~3.2M sq ft, ~1,500 jobs initially cited) in Sherman, Texas. Most recent status: the facility held its grand opening on May 15, 2025 and is ramping 300mm wafer production at low volume, with a further ~$4B expansion in planning as of early 2026.

Air Products announced on Oct 14, 2021 a ~$4.5B blue hydrogen/blue ammonia Louisiana Clean Energy Complex (with carbon capture) in Ascension Parish, Louisiana. Most recent status: Air Products disclosed in a June 30, 2026 SEC filing that it will NOT proceed with the project (cancelled), taking a pre-tax write-down not exceeding ~$2.9B; costs had ballooned toward ~$9B and the in-service date had slipped from 2026 to 2028-2029 before cancellation.

ArcelorMittal announced on Feb 6, 2025 a ~$1.2B (gross; ~$0.9B net of government support) new non-grain-oriented electrical steel (NOES) manufacturing facility (up to 150Kt/yr, for EV motors) at its Calvert site in Mobile County, Alabama. Most recent status: per ArcelorMittal's FY2025 annual report (year ended Dec 31, 2025), the plant is under construction with major process-equipment manufacturing commenced and production targeted for 2H 2027; the supporting 1.5Mt Calvert EAF is ramping toward full capacity in mid-2026.

Steel Dynamics announced on Nov 2, 2022 a greenfield recycled-aluminum flat-rolled mill (650,000 metric tons/yr, ~700 direct jobs; investment cited ~$1.9B-$2.5B) at the KCS Infinity megasite in Columbus, Lowndes County, Mississippi. This is an aluminum (non-steel metals) manufacturing facility -> 'other' sector. Most recent status: per Steel Dynamics' Q2 2026 results (quarter ended Jun 30, 2026), the mill is ramping -- 53,000 metric tons of flat-rolled shipments in Q2 2026, two of three cold mills operational with the third commissioning in July 2026 to reach full 650kt capacity, automotive qualifications achieved and automotive sales expected before end of 2026.

Ford announced on Feb 13, 2023 BlueOval Battery Park Michigan, a ~$3.5B greenfield lithium iron phosphate (LFP) EV battery cell-and-pack plant (~35 GWh, ~2,500 jobs at announcement) on a 950-acre site in Marshall, Calhoun County, Michigan. Most recent status (as of June 2026 reporting): the plant is in pilot production with its first regular LFP battery cells expected later in 2026; Ford scaled the project back in Nov 2024 (to ~$3B, ~1,700 jobs, reduced tax credits, and shifted some output toward residential energy storage).

First Solar announced a ~$1.1B photovoltaic solar module manufacturing facility (3.5 GW/yr, 700+ direct jobs) at the Mallard Fox West Industrial Complex in Trinity, Lawrence County, Alabama on Nov 16, 2022. Most recent status: the plant was inaugurated in September 2024 and is now operational and producing panels (its fourth U.S. factory; distinct from First Solar's separately-announced Iberia Parish, Louisiana plant).

Bristol Myers Squibb announced on Aug 10, 2026 a new ~$2.3B multi-modal pharmaceutical manufacturing campus (~600,000 sq ft; small molecules, biologics and antibody-drug conjugates; ~500 permanent direct jobs) at Generation Park in Houston, Texas. Most recent status (as of Aug 2026): just announced/early planning stage, with construction anticipated 2027-2030 and completion targeted for 2030 — not yet under construction.

Envision AESC announced on Apr 13, 2022 a ~$2B lithium-ion EV battery gigafactory (30 GWh, ~2,000 full-time direct jobs) at the Kentucky Transpark in Bowling Green, Warren County, Kentucky, breaking ground Aug 2022. Most recent status (June 2025): construction of the Bowling Green plant is continuing and the company reaffirmed the $2B/2,000-job commitment, even as its separate South Carolina facility had construction paused; Bowling Green targeted to be operational in 2027 (not yet producing).

Bosch announced in 2023 an investment (originally ~$1.5B, later scaled to ~$1.9-2B) to transform its Roseville, California site (assets acquired from TSI Semiconductors) into a 200mm silicon-carbide (SiC) semiconductor fabrication facility for EV power chips (~700 direct manufacturing/engineering jobs; clears the floor on capital). Most recent status (July 2026): Bosch finalized an up-to-$225M CHIPS Act direct-funding agreement, has begun sample production, and targets its first commercial 200mm SiC production chips in 2026 (~300 associates on site so far; not yet at commercial volume).

Hyundai Motor Group and SK On announced a 50/50 joint-venture (Hyundai-SK Battery Manufacturing America) ~$5B lithium-ion EV battery cell plant (35 GWh, 3.3M sq ft, ~3,500-3,750 direct jobs) in Bartow County (Cartersville), Georgia, first announced by Gov. Kemp in Dec 2022 and formalized in 2023 (a distinct site from Hyundai's Metaplant America assembly plant in Bryan County). Most recent status (July 2026): the plant has opened and begun initial battery-cell production, described as the early stages of production with plans to gradually scale up.

GlobalFoundries announced on Feb 19, 2024 a >$11.6B major expansion of its Fab 8 semiconductor site in Malta, Saratoga County, New York (new 358,000-sq-ft 300mm fab plus advanced packaging, ~1,500 direct jobs). Most recent status (Manufacturing Dive, Jun 4, 2025): GF raised its total U.S. commitment to $16B and reports an advanced packaging/testing center under construction on the Malta campus.

Amgen announced on Dec 5, 2024 a ~$1B second drug-substance (biologics) manufacturing facility at its Holly Springs, North Carolina campus (~370 direct jobs; clears the floor on capital). Most recent status found (Carolina Journal, Jan 2025): Amgen broke ground and began construction on this second plant on Jan 24, 2025, while opening its first Holly Springs facility.

General Motors announced on Jan 25, 2022 a ~$4B conversion of its Orion Assembly plant in Lake Orion (Orion Township), Michigan to electric full-size pickup truck production (part of a $7B Michigan package; ~4,000 new plus ~1,000 retained jobs). Most recent status (Oakland County Times, Jun 11, 2025): GM repurposed the plant — Orion will instead build gas-powered full-size SUVs and light-duty pickups beginning 2027, with EV truck production shifted to Factory ZERO in Detroit-Hamtramck.

Graphic Packaging International announced in early 2023 a ~$1B greenfield coated recycled paperboard (CRB) mill on a 119-acre campus in Waco, McLennan County, Texas (640,000 sq ft, ~230 direct jobs; clears the floor on capital). Most recent status (Packaging Dive, Nov 4, 2025): the mill began operating ahead of schedule, producing its first commercially saleable rolls in October 2025, with full production expected within 12-18 months.

GM and LG Energy Solution (JV Ultium Cells LLC) announced on Apr 16, 2021 a >$2.3B lithium-ion EV battery cell plant in Spring Hill, Maury County, Tennessee (~2.8M sq ft, ~1,300 direct jobs) - their 2nd U.S. Ultium plant and a distinct site from the Lordstown, Ohio JV plant. Most recent status (electrive, Mar 20, 2026): the plant has operated since 2024 producing NMCA cells and is being retrofitted (~$70M) to also make LFP cells for stationary energy storage.

LG Chem announced on Nov 21, 2022 a ~$3.2B battery cathode (NCMA) manufacturing plant in Clarksville, Montgomery County, Tennessee (~860 direct jobs), its first US cathode facility. Most recent status: groundbreaking held Dec 2023; as of the latest reporting (late 2023/early 2024) construction was underway with mass production targeted for 2026 — no newer credible update found.

Regeneron announced on Nov 21, 2025 a ~$2B biologics drug-manufacturing plant at the former Quad Graphics site (56 Duplainville Road, ~1.1M sq ft) in Saratoga Springs, Saratoga County, New York (~1,000 direct jobs), roughly doubling its NY manufacturing capacity. Most recent status: just announced/planned as of late Nov 2025; the site was acquired and selected for a federal FDA fast-track pilot; construction not yet begun.

Shintech (Shin-Etsu) announced on Jan 26, 2021 a ~$1.25B major expansion of its Plaquemine PVC/chlor-alkali/vinyl chloride monomer plant in Iberville Parish, Louisiana (part of a $1.3B package including Addis). Most recent status: independent trade reporting in March 2026 states this ~$1.25B expansion was completed/wrapped up in 2024 (producing). Distinct from Shintech's separate, later ~$3.4B Plaquemine expansion announced March 2026.

Texas Instruments announced on Feb 15, 2023 a ~$11B new 300-mm analog/embedded semiconductor wafer fab (LFAB2, ~800 direct jobs) in Lehi, Utah, adjacent to its existing Lehi fab. A distinct site from TI's Sherman, Texas fabs. Most recent status: broke ground Nov 2, 2023; as of 2025-2026 reporting the fab is under construction and on track for initial production in 2026, with no delays reported.

General Motors announced in late January 2020 a ~$2.2B conversion of its Detroit-Hamtramck assembly plant into 'Factory ZERO', a dedicated EV assembly plant in Detroit/Hamtramck, Michigan (~2,200 direct jobs). A distinct site from GM's listed Orion Assembly conversion. Most recent status (as of March 2026): production began in 2021 (Hummer EV, then Silverado EV, Sierra EV, Cadillac Escalade IQ), but the plant has seen near-continuous disruption since mid-2025 — repeated multi-week production pauses (latest ~Mar 16-Apr 13, 2026), ~1,140 jobs eliminated in 2025, and the next-gen full-size electric-truck program delayed indefinitely amid weak EV demand.

Our Next Energy (ONE) announced a ~$1.6B lithium-ion 'ONE Circle' battery cell gigafactory (20 GWh, 2,112 direct jobs) in Van Buren Township (Wayne County), Michigan on Oct 5, 2022; production was promised to begin 2024 and scale to full capacity by end of 2027. Most recent status (Detroit News, Jan 21, 2026): ONE lost its largest EV customer's contract, cut ~45% of staff, suspended EV-battery investment to pivot toward rail/defense/grid storage, and is in talks to vacate roughly two-thirds of the Van Buren plant; the MEDC has stopped further incentive payments.

Eli Lilly announced on Sep 23, 2025 a new ~$6.5B active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) manufacturing facility on a 236-acre site at Generation Park in Houston, Harris County, Texas, with ~615 permanent direct jobs; it is the second of four new U.S. Lilly manufacturing sites announced in 2025 and is targeted to be operational by ~2030. Most recent status (Community Impact, reporting on July 2026 Texas TDLR filings): site earthwork/construction has begun, with several associated projects underway or starting August 2026 and foundations/steel expected to rise late 2026-2027; Lilly says the overall project remains on track for completion by 2030.

Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) announced on May 15, 2025 a ~$4B primary aluminum smelter (initially ~600,000 t/yr, ~1,000 direct jobs) at the Tulsa Port of Inola in Rogers County, Oklahoma — the first new U.S. primary aluminum smelter since 1980; construction was expected to begin around end of 2026 with production by the end of the decade. Most recent status (Manufacturing Dive, Aug 2026): Century Aluminum has joined as a 40% JV partner (EGA 60%), the plant was upsized to ~750,000 t/yr, detailed engineering is underway and an air permit was filed, but Oklahoma AG Gentner Drummond sued on June 2, 2026 and in Aug 2026 moved for a preliminary injunction to block the project on anticipatory-public-nuisance/pollution grounds, while the U.S. DOJ filed a statement of interest supporting the project.

Wanhua Chemical (US) announced a ~$1.25B MDI / isocyanates (polyurethane) manufacturing complex (400 kt/yr MDI, ~170 direct jobs) in Convent, St. James Parish, Louisiana, first announced in 2017 and with the Convent site confirmed in 2018 (clears the size floor on capital, not jobs). Most recent credible status is old but terminal (WWLTV, Sep 2019 — the latest available for this site): Wanhua withdrew its St. James Parish land-use permit application and dropped the Convent project amid rising costs, U.S.-China tariffs and sustained community/environmental opposition; the complex was never built and, as of 2026, no revival at this site is documented.

Intel announced in March 2021 (its 'IDM 2.0' strategy) a ~$20B investment to build two new leading-edge semiconductor fabs, Fab 52 and Fab 62, at its Ocotillo campus in Chandler, Arizona, creating more than 3,000 direct jobs; groundbreaking was Sep 24, 2021 and the fabs were originally targeted to be operational in 2024. This is a distinct Arizona site from Intel's separately announced Ohio 'Silicon Heartland' campus. Most recent status (DataCenterDynamics, reporting Intel's late-2025/2026 disclosures): Fab 52 became fully operational in October 2025 as Intel's first high-volume Intel 18A fab (~10,000 wafer starts/week), producing Panther Lake compute tiles and, in H1 2026, Clearwater Forest server chips; 18A yields are still ramping toward industry-standard levels (targeted early 2027), so part of Fab 52's capacity is currently held idle.

Micron Technology announced on Aug 29, 2018 a ~$3B expansion of its Manassas, Virginia DRAM/memory fab, adding ~1,100 direct jobs (state's largest private capital investment at the time). Most recent status (May 22, 2026): the Manassas fab began 1-alpha (1a) DRAM production - the most advanced memory made in the U.S. - now supporting ~3,100 direct jobs.

OCI Global announced in Nov 2022 (construction start; groundbreaking Dec 2022) a world-scale ~1.1 million-t/yr hydrogen-based 'blue' ammonia plant with carbon capture (KBR/Linde technology) in Beaumont, Texas; the project was later valued at ~$2.35B in its Aug 2024 sale to Woodside Energy. Most recent status (Mar 25, 2026): the facility completed performance testing, is producing ammonia, and was formally handed over to Woodside.

General Motors and Samsung SDI announced on Apr 25, 2023 a more-than-$3B (later ~$3.5B) joint-venture EV battery cell plant, subsequently sited in New Carlisle, Indiana (680 acres; ~1,600 direct jobs; ~27-36 GWh). Most recent status (Aug 11, 2026): Samsung SDI acquired GM's ~50% stake to take full ownership, with mass production targeted for 2027 (delayed from 2026) and the plant pivoting toward energy-storage-system cells amid slower EV demand.

Albemarle announced on Mar 22, 2023 a ~$1.3B 'Mega-Flex' lithium hydroxide processing plant (~50,000 t/yr battery-grade lithium hydroxide, expandable to 100,000 t/yr; ~300 direct jobs) near Richburg, Chester County, South Carolina. Most recent credible status (Mar 18, 2024): Albemarle paused the project, deferring the planned 2024 groundbreaking amid a lithium-price collapse; no credible source confirms a restart since, so this Mar-2024 pause is the latest verified status.

FREYR Battery announced 'Giga America,' a greenfield lithium-ion battery cell gigafactory in Coweta County (Newnan), Georgia, on Nov 11, 2022 (~$1.7B initial first phase, up to ~$2.6B total by 2029, ~720 direct jobs). Most recent status (Feb 2025, latest found): FREYR, since rebranded T1 Energy, cancelled the project and sold the 368-acre site for $50M, pivoting to solar; the plant was never built.

Natron Energy announced on Aug 15, 2024 a ~$1.4B greenfield giga-scale sodium-ion battery manufacturing facility (24 GWh) at the Kingsboro Megasite in Edgecombe County, North Carolina (1,000+ direct jobs). Most recent status (Sept 2025, latest found): Natron Energy ceased all operations on Sept 3, 2025 after failing to raise sufficient funding, cancelling the North Carolina gigafactory before construction.

American Battery Factory announced on Dec 6, 2022 its first U.S. lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery cell gigafactory (~$1.2B capital investment, ~2M sq ft) in Tucson (Pima County), Arizona, and broke ground in Oct 2023. Most recent status (March 2026, latest found): ABF secured 4.5+ GWh of binding offtake and was finalizing plant financing, with production now slated to begin in late 2027 (delayed from the initial 2025 first-phase target).

Ultium Cells (GM-LG Energy Solution JV) announced on Jan 26, 2022 a ~$2.6B lithium-ion EV battery cell plant (its third U.S. plant, ~2.8M sq ft, ~1,700 jobs at full operation) in Delta Township near Lansing, Michigan. GM exited its stake in 2024; LG Energy Solution announced the start of production (LFP energy-storage and NMC EV cells; ~900 employees, targeting 35+ GWh) on Aug 18, 2026 -- the most recent status.

Intel announced on May 3, 2021 a ~$3.5B expansion of its Rio Rancho, New Mexico campus (Fab 9) to manufacture advanced semiconductor packaging, including its Foveros 3D packaging technology (~700 direct high-tech jobs). Most recent status: Intel opened Fab 9 on Jan 24, 2024, described as its first co-located operational site for mass production of Foveros 3D advanced packaging (Fab 9 packaging + Fab 11X). Distinct facility from Intel's Arizona and Ohio fabs.

Toyota announced on Feb 6, 2024 a ~$1.3B investment at its Georgetown, Kentucky (TMMK) plant to assemble an all-new three-row battery-electric SUV (Highlander EV) and add a battery-pack assembly line -- its first U.S.-assembled BEV. Most recent status (Electrek, Sept 3, 2026): production had not yet started, delayed to January 2027 at the earliest.

BMW Group announced on Oct 19, 2022 a $1.7B South Carolina EV investment, of which ~$1B is to prepare its existing Plant Spartanburg to build fully electric vehicles (a separate $700M high-voltage battery-assembly plant is planned in Woodruff, SC). Anchored on the ~$1B Plant Spartanburg EV expansion. Most recent status (BMW Group press release, June 30, 2026): the $1.7B investment is complete and assembly of the fully electric iX5 -- the first all-electric BMW built in the U.S. -- is scheduled to begin at Plant Spartanburg before the end of 2026.

Eastman announced on March 25, 2024 a ~$1.2-1.3B second U.S. molecular recycling (methanolysis) facility in Longview, Texas (~110,000 t/yr of hard-to-recycle plastic, ~200 direct jobs; clears the floor on capital). As of the most recent reporting (April 9, 2026) the project is on hold/under review after the DOE revoked a $375M grant in May 2025; Eastman is reassessing scope, timing and location.

KORE Power announced its KOREPlex lithium-ion battery cell gigafactory in Buckeye, Arizona (~2M sq ft, ~12 GWh/yr, ~$1.25B investment and 3,000+ permanent jobs; 214-acre site purchased April 2022, construction started 2022). As of the most recent credible reporting (Feb 6, 2025) the project was cancelled/shelved: KORE said it 'will not move forward at this time,' the site was listed for sale, the founder/CEO stepped down, a contractor filed a ~$10.4M lien, and the promised $850M DOE loan never closed.

ExxonMobil announced (FEED awarded Jan 30, 2023) a world-scale low-carbon 'blue' hydrogen, ammonia and carbon-capture facility at its Baytown, Texas complex: ~1 billion cubic feet/day of hydrogen with >98% CO2 capture (~7 Mt/yr) plus low-carbon ammonia, estimated ~$7B, startup targeted 2027-2029. As of the most recent reporting (Dec 1, 2025) ExxonMobil has paused/scrapped the project, citing an inability to secure offtake customers and the withdrawal of federal (DOE) support in spring 2025.

Nutrien announced on May 18, 2022 an ~$2B clean ('blue') ammonia manufacturing facility at Geismar, Louisiana (1.2 million tonnes/yr, billed as the world's largest, with >=90% CO2 capture of ~1.8 Mt/yr); FID was expected in 2023, construction in 2024 and full production by 2027. As of the most recent reporting (June 12, 2024) Nutrien formally cancelled the project (after halting work indefinitely in 2023), citing rising costs and uncertain clean-ammonia demand while refocusing on its core agriculture business.

Enel North America, through affiliate 3Sun USA, announced on May 22, 2023 a >$1B solar PV cell-and-module gigafactory at the Tulsa Port of Inola, Oklahoma: ~3 GW/yr of heterojunction (HJT) cells and panels in a 2M+ sq ft plant, ~1,000 direct permanent jobs by 2025 (scalable to 6 GW and ~900 more jobs). Most-recent-status note: the freshest credible reporting I could locate is Oklahoma Energy Today (Nov 19, 2024), which reports the project on hold - work stalled in spring 2024 and Enel's new CEO said it would proceed only if a U.S. investor took a majority stake; I could not find any 2025-2026 update, so this on-hold status is as of late 2024.

Genentech (Roche) announced on May 12, 2025 a new drug-substance biologics manufacturing facility (~700,000 sq ft; next-generation obesity/metabolic medicines) in Holly Springs, Wake County, North Carolina, its first East Coast plant; the investment was later expanded to ~$2B (Jan 2026). This is a distinct site from the Amgen and Fujifilm Diosynth facilities in the same town. Most recent status: topped out (structural framework complete) on Aug 18, 2026, with completion expected in 2029.

Boeing announced (late 2024) and broke ground on Nov 7, 2025 on a more-than-$1B expansion of its North Charleston, South Carolina 787 Dreamliner campus, a new ~1.2M-sq-ft final assembly building (~1,000 new direct jobs) to raise 787 output to 10 aircraft/month. Most recent status: under construction; steel erection on the new final assembly building began Apr 2026 and vertical construction was progressing as of mid-2026.

Tesla announced on Jan 23, 2023 a ~$3.6B expansion of Gigafactory Nevada in Storey County (Sparks), Nevada, adding two new plants: a 100 GWh 4680 battery cell factory and its first high-volume Tesla Semi factory (~4M sq ft added, ~3,000 new direct jobs). Most recent status: Tesla Semi high-volume production began in Nevada, with the first truck reported off the high-volume line on Apr 29, 2026; 4680 cells are produced on-site in the same complex.

Lake Charles Methanol II announced in Feb 2024 a ~$3.24B greenfield low-carbon ('blue') methanol plant (~3.6M tonnes/yr) at the Port of Lake Charles, Louisiana. Most recent status (Nov 2025): still pre-construction, FEED contract awarded to Zachry Group and permitting complete, with the final investment decision now expected Q2 2026 and construction start targeted Q4 2026 (the FID was originally slated for mid-2024).

Gotion Inc. announced in Sept 2023 a ~$2B lithium-ion battery manufacturing plant (LFP cells/packs; ~2,600 projected direct jobs) in Manteno, Kankakee County, Illinois, a different site from its Green Charter Township, Michigan facility. Most recent status (Nov 2025): tracking well below the announced plan, ~300 employees (target 450 by end-2025, 1,400 in 2026), running five assembly lines in a converted 1.5M-sq-ft former Kmart warehouse producing commercial/residential energy-storage units.

Stellantis committed (as part of its late-2023 UAW agreement) to reopen its idled Belvidere, Illinois auto assembly plant to build a new mid-size pickup/next-gen Jeep Cherokee, a >$600M (later raised to ~$800M) investment restoring roughly 3,300 jobs. As of the most recent update (Aug 14, 2026), retooling work is underway but pilot production has slipped to first-half 2028 and retail production to second-half 2029.

Texas Instruments announced on Apr 18, 2019 a ~$3.1B second 300mm analog/embedded semiconductor wafer fab (RFAB2, ~488 direct jobs) in Richardson, Texas. RFAB2 began initial production on Sept 29, 2022; per TI's most recent facility page, both Richardson fabs (RFAB1 and RFAB2) are now in production and ramping toward full volume (this is the freshest status located).

Cleveland-Cliffs announced on Mar 25, 2024 a ~$1.6B project (including a ~$500M U.S. DOE grant) to replace the coal blast furnace at its Middletown Works in Middletown, Ohio with a hydrogen-ready ~2.5 Mtpa Direct Reduced Iron plant plus two electric melting furnaces (near-zero-emissions 'green steel'). Most recent status (Mar 27, 2026 reporting): Cliffs abandoned the hydrogen/DRI plan and, per a late-Feb 2026 Ohio EPA air-permit filing, now intends to refurbish the existing coal blast furnace and add a waste-gas cogeneration plant; the DOE grant reportedly remains intact but its revised use is unresolved.

Rivian and the State of Illinois announced on May 2, 2024 a ~$1.5B expansion of Rivian's existing Normal, Illinois EV assembly plant to add production of its R2 SUV, raising site capacity to ~215,000 units/yr and creating 550+ new full-time jobs. Most recent status (May 19, 2026): the first R2 rolled off the Normal line in April 2026 and production is ramping with accelerated hiring toward a full R2 run rate of up to ~155,000 units/yr.

Leprino Foods announced in 2022 an ~$1 billion greenfield 850,000-sq-ft mozzarella cheese and dairy-nutrition manufacturing plant in East Lubbock, Texas (described by Lubbock EDA as the city's largest-ever private investment; ~600 full-time jobs at full build). Most recent verifiable status (Jan 2025): the plant opened its first phase and began production, initially staffing ~300, with a second phase slated to bring total employment to ~600 by 2026 — no credible update more recent than early 2025 was located.

Redwood Materials announced on Dec 14-15, 2022 a ~$3.5B battery-materials campus (anode/cathode component manufacturing plus recycling; ~1,500 direct jobs; ~100 GWh/yr capacity) at Camp Hall Commerce Park in Berkeley County (Ridgeville), South Carolina - a distinct site from its Nevada campus. Clears the floor on capital. Most recent status (Redwood release, Nov 6, 2025, read via browser UA after a 403): first operations are online at the SC campus, adding an initial 20,000 metric tons/yr of critical-materials recovery/production; buildout is phased over the next decade.

LG Energy Solution announced on Mar 22, 2022 a ~$1.7B major expansion of its lithium-ion EV battery plant in Holland, Michigan (~1,200 new direct jobs; capacity from 5 GWh toward ~25 GWh) - a distinct site from LGES's Queen Creek AZ, Clarksville/Montgomery TN and Ultium plants. Clears the floor on capital. Most recent status (CleanTechnica, Jun 28, 2025; corroborated by WardsAuto/Canary Media June 2025): the Holland plant pivoted toward LFP cells for grid/ESS storage as EV demand cooled and began LFP production in May 2025 (16.5 GWh ESS lines, two of three lines operating), while also onshoring NMC cells for the Ford Mustang Mach-E.

Clean Hydrogen Works (with partners Denbury, Hafnia, Mitsui O.S.K. Lines and ExxonMobil) proposed in 2022 the ~$7.5B Ascension Clean Energy (ACE) project, a greenfield world-scale low-carbon 'blue' ammonia complex (up to ~7.1-7.2M tonnes/yr with carbon capture; ~350 direct jobs) at the RiverPlex MegaPark near Donaldsonville, Ascension Parish, Louisiana - distinct from the listed Air Products, CF Industries Blue Point, Nutrien and Methanex Louisiana projects. Clears the floor on capital. Most recent status (Louisiana Illuminator, Feb 10, 2026, read via browser UA after a 403): the plant remains a proposed, pre-construction project awaiting a final investment decision (FID expected ~early 2026, construction to start thereafter); no commercial-scale blue ammonia plants are yet operating.

St. Charles Clean Fuels (a JV of Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners, which holds the majority stake, and Sustainable Fuels Group) proposed in 2023 a ~$4.6B greenfield reduced-carbon ('blue') ammonia production-and-export facility (two 4,000 MTD trains, ~2.8-3.0M tonnes/yr, >90% CO2 capture; ~216 direct jobs) on a ~230-acre IMTT site at St. Rose, St. Charles Parish, Louisiana - distinct from the listed Air Products, CF Industries Blue Point, Nutrien, Methanex and Clean Hydrogen Works LA projects. Clears the floor on capital. Most recent status: this remains a proposed, pre-construction project - the CIP project page (read via the Wayback Machine snapshot dated 2026-06-10, as cip.com's live page 404s) still lists 'final investment decision expected end-2024; operational from 2027,' an FID target that has lapsed with no publicly confirmed FID or groundbreaking; independent reporting (WWNO, Aug 2024) likewise described it as still in permitting/proposed.

Southern Energy Renewables announced on Mar 11, 2026 its ~$1.4B first commercial-scale U.S. facility - a greenfield plant to convert regional wood-waste biomass into green methanol and sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) (~120 direct jobs) in St. Charles Parish, Louisiana. Clears the floor on capital; sector is chemicals/renewable fuels ('other'). Most recent status (LED and Hydrocarbon Processing, both Mar 2026): newly announced and pre-construction - construction is planned to begin in late 2027 with commercial operation targeted for late 2029; no ground broken yet. Because the project was just announced, the promise and current-status sources coincide at the March 2026 announcement.

Ascend Elements announced on Aug 1, 2022 its Apex 1 EV battery materials plant (lithium-ion cathode precursor / pCAM) at Commerce Industrial Park II in Hopkinsville, Christian County, Kentucky - a $310M Phase 1 within an up-to-$1B multi-phase investment (~400 jobs). Most recent status (Christian County Now, June 30, 2026): after an early-2026 Chapter 11 bankruptcy, the roughly 50%-built plant was sold at a bankruptcy auction to a Turner-Kokosing joint venture for $31.7M and is not operational; new owners are seeking a buyer to finish it.

Mercedes-Benz announced on Sep 21, 2017 a ~$1B expansion of its Alabama operations - electric-vehicle (EQ-brand SUV) production at its Vance/Tuscaloosa County assembly plant plus a new lithium-ion battery plant in Bibb County (~600 new jobs). Most recent status (Yahoo Autos, Jan 21, 2026): the Tuscaloosa plant has assembled the all-electric EQS SUV since 2022 and also builds the EQE SUV and Maybach EQS SUV, with battery packs supplied by the operating Bibb County battery plant.

Air Products and AES announced on Dec 8, 2022 plans to invest ~$4B to build what was billed as the largest U.S. green hydrogen production facility (~1.4 GW of wind and solar power plus electrolyzers producing >200 metric tons/day of green hydrogen) in Wilbarger County, Texas, targeted for commercial operation in 2027. Most recent status (Vernon Daily Record, Nov 21, 2024 - the latest available update): the joint venture dissolved after Air Products withdrew in November 2024, unable to reach a final investment decision; the plant has not been built.

Fiat Chrysler (now Stellantis) announced on Feb 26, 2019 a $1.6B conversion of its Mack Avenue Engine Complex into a new Detroit, Michigan auto assembly plant - the city's first new assembly plant in nearly three decades - to build the next-gen Jeep Grand Cherokee and an all-new three-row Jeep SUV, adding ~3,850 direct jobs. Most recent status (CBT News, Apr 22, 2025): the plant (Detroit Assembly Complex - Mack) opened and has built the Jeep Grand Cherokee L / Grand Cherokee since 2021, but is running production pauses and layoffs amid an ~11% year-over-year Grand Cherokee sales decline while transitioning to the refreshed 2026 model.

Eli Lilly announced on Dec 6, 2024 a ~$3B expansion of its recently acquired parenteral (injectable) drug manufacturing facility in Pleasant Prairie, Kenosha County, Wisconsin (~750 direct jobs; brings total planned WI investment to ~$4B). Most recent status (2025 / early-2026 reporting): final Village of Pleasant Prairie approvals granted March 2025 and full-scale construction underway, with additions projected complete around March 2026 and production expected to ramp from late 2025; no source yet confirms first commercial output as of this collection.

Hyundai Motor Group and LG Energy Solution announced their HL-GA Battery Company joint venture, a lithium-ion EV battery cell plant (30 GWh/yr, ~3,000 direct jobs), which they expanded to a more-than-$4.3B investment on Aug 31, 2023 (JV first announced May 2023) at the Bryan County / Ellabell megasite near Savannah, Georgia. This is the separate battery-cell JV facility (distinct entity and building), not the co-located Hyundai Metaplant vehicle-assembly plant. Most recent status (Nov 14, 2025 reporting): construction resumed after a Sept 4, 2025 federal immigration raid halted work for ~two months, and the JV reaffirmed a first-half-2026 production start, so the plant is not yet producing as of this collection.

Monolith Materials announced (~Nov 2020) a ~$1B expansion, 'Olive Creek 2' (OC2), of its methane-pyrolysis plant near Hallam, Nebraska, to make carbon black and low-carbon anhydrous ammonia, with hundreds of direct manufacturing jobs and commercial operation originally targeted by Dec 31, 2025. Most recent status (notchconsulting, ~March 2026): the project was optimized/scaled to four production units (~220,000 t/yr carbon black) after Monolith lost its conditional ~$1.04B U.S. DOE Title XVII loan guarantee, and construction had not yet begun — the company said it plans to start construction later in 2026, so OC2 is not yet producing as of this collection.

Eli Lilly announced on Sep 16, 2025 a ~$5B fully integrated active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) and drug-product plant for its bioconjugate/monoclonal-antibody (oncology) portfolio at West Creek Business Park in Goochland County, Virginia (~650 direct jobs, ~1,800 construction jobs). This is a distinct Virginia site, separate from Lilly's other newly announced U.S. sites. Most recent status (Richmond BizSense, July 23, 2026): Lilly paid ~$38.4M for a 227-acre West Creek parcel, but site work had not begun and the plan of development was still pending with Goochland County (a required Dominion transmission line was also awaiting SCC approval as of June 2026) — the plant is not yet producing as of this collection.

Eli Lilly announced on Dec 9, 2025 a more-than-$6B active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) facility to make small-molecule synthetic and peptide medicines (including its oral GLP-1 orforglipron) on a ~260-acre Greenbrier site in Huntsville, Limestone County, Alabama (~450 direct jobs; ~3,000 construction jobs). This is a distinct Alabama site, the third of four new U.S. Lilly plants, separate from Lilly's Virginia, Wisconsin and other announced facilities. Most recent status: as of the Dec 2025 announcement (the freshest reporting available at this collection), construction was slated to begin in 2026 with completion targeted for 2032; the plant is not yet under construction or producing.

Lyten announced on Oct 15, 2024 a >$1B lithium-sulfur battery gigafactory (1.25M sq ft, up to 10 GWh/yr, ~1,000 eventual jobs) at the Reno AirLogistics Park in Stead, Nevada. As of late January 2026 the project has been cancelled: Lyten could not negotiate a lease with the Reno-Tahoe Airport Authority and pivoted to acquiring existing (ex-Northvolt) European plants instead.

Yara Clean Ammonia and Enbridge announced on Mar 31, 2023 (through JV Ingleside Clean Ammonia Partners) 'Project YaREN,' a world-scale low-carbon ('blue') ammonia plant with carbon capture (~2.8M t/yr across two units, ~US$2.6-2.9B per unit, ~200 permanent jobs) at the Enbridge Ingleside Energy Center near Corpus Christi / Ingleside, Texas. Most recent status (early December 2025): still in local permitting - the Ingleside City Council approved the first reading of a special use permit 4-2 in November 2025, with a second reading set for Dec 9, 2025; no final investment decision or construction start yet.

Analog Devices (ADI) announced on July 26, 2023 a more-than-$1B expansion of its Beaverton, Oregon semiconductor wafer fab (ADI's largest fab by volume; expanding cleanroom to ~118,000 sq ft, converting to a full 200mm/8-inch line for 180nm-and-above nodes and roughly doubling internal capacity, adding hundreds of jobs to ~950 existing Oregon employees). Most recent status (Jan 16, 2025): the expansion is proceeding - the U.S. Commerce Department signed a non-binding CHIPS Act memorandum for up to $105M toward ADI expansions at Beaverton plus Camas, WA and Chelmsford, MA (~500 jobs across the sites), with ADI stating its 'most significant' investment is at Beaverton; no delays reported.

ENTEK announced on Mar 22, 2023 a $1.5B (later cited ~$1.7B) greenfield lithium-ion battery separator manufacturing plant (four buildings, ~1.4M sq ft, up to ~642 direct jobs) on a 340-acre site in Vigo County Industrial Park II, Terre Haute, Indiana. Most recent status (September 2025): construction proceeding - the U.S. Department of Energy disbursed the first ~$77M of an up-to-$1.3B DOE loan, I Squared Capital is investing ~$800M for a majority equity stake, and Phase I start of production is targeted for Q4 2026.

AbbVie announced on April 22, 2026 a $1.4B new pharmaceutical manufacturing campus (185 acres near Research Triangle Park; ~734 permanent jobs; first-phase small-volume parenteral / sterile-injectable drug-product manufacturing plus next-generation labs and warehouse, supporting its immunology, neuroscience and oncology medicines) in Durham, North Carolina - described as AbbVie's largest-ever single-campus capital investment. Most recent status (as of the April 22, 2026 announcement, corroborated by the NC Governor/Commerce release the same day): pre-construction - construction is slated to begin in 2026 with completion expected by the end of 2028; no groundbreaking reported yet.

DENSO announced on Oct 6, 2017 a $1 billion expansion of its DENSO Manufacturing Tennessee (DMTN) plant in Maryville, Blount County, Tennessee, to make the site a North American hub for vehicle electrification (EV inverters) and advanced safety systems, adding ~1,000 direct jobs. Current status (per DENSO's DMTN company page, reflecting operations as of 2025): the Maryville plant is operating and producing inverters/electronics, with roughly 4,500 employees across DENSO's Tennessee sites.

Diamond Green Diesel (a 50/50 JV of Darling Ingredients and Valero Energy) announced in January 2021 board approval to build a new ~$1.45 billion renewable diesel plant (~470 million gal/yr) adjacent to Valero's Port Arthur, Texas refinery. Most recent status found (biofuels press reporting dated Jan 2024): the plant began operations in late 2022 and is producing renewable diesel, with a $315M sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) upgrade then expected to complete in Q1 2025 — no more recent operational update was located, so status is as of early 2024/2025 reporting.

NOVONIX announced on Dec 16, 2024 a new ~$1 billion greenfield synthetic graphite manufacturing plant ('NOVONIX Enterprise South') in the Enterprise South Industrial Park, Chattanooga (Hamilton County), Tennessee — ~31,500 tonnes/yr of battery-anode synthetic graphite, ~500 direct jobs, supported by a conditional US$754.8M U.S. Department of Energy loan. Most recent status found (NOVONIX release dated Jan 2025): intended site selected with a land purchase-and-sale agreement with the City of Chattanooga and Hamilton County pending approvals; full production targeted by end of 2028. No more recent update was located, so status is as of early 2025.

Amplify Cell Technologies (a joint venture of Accelera by Cummins, Daimler Truck and PACCAR) announced a greenfield lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) battery cell factory in Marshall County (Byhalia), Mississippi — ~2 million sq ft, ~21 GWh/yr capacity, more than 2,000 direct manufacturing jobs (called the largest payroll commitment in state history). The Mississippi site was selected/announced in 2023 and the JV broke ground in 2024. Most recent status (electrive, dated Oct 22, 2025): the start of battery cell production has been postponed from 2027 to 2028.

Merck announced a ~$3B 'Center of Excellence' for pharmaceutical (active pharmaceutical ingredient and small-molecule drug-product) manufacturing at its existing Elkton, Rockingham County, Virginia site, breaking ground on Oct 20, 2025 (~500 permanent jobs, 400,000 sq ft; scaled up from an earlier ~$2B/300-job plan). Most recent status (as of the Oct 20, 2025 groundbreaking, the freshest reporting found): under construction, with completion targeted for 2029 and initial production expected around 2028 — not yet producing.

Saronic Technologies announced on July 16, 2026 'Port Alpha,' a more-than-$3B next-generation shipyard to mass-produce autonomous/unmanned naval vessels at the Port of Brownsville, Cameron County, Texas (initial 835 acres, up to ~4,400; up to 10,000 direct jobs). Most recent status (as of the July 2026 site-selection announcement, the freshest reporting found): site selected, construction anticipated to begin in 2026 with operations targeted for 2028 — not yet under construction or producing.

Toyota Motor North America announced on July 6, 2026 a ~$3.6B expansion of its San Antonio, Texas assembly plant (Toyota Texas), adding a second vehicle assembly line for the Tacoma pickup (~2.5M sq ft added; ~2,000 new direct jobs) and shifting Tacoma production from Baja California, Mexico. Most recent status (as of the July 2026 announcement, the freshest reporting found): announced/planning stage, with the new line scheduled to begin operations in 2030 — not yet under construction or producing.

U.S. Steel (following Nippon Steel's 2025 acquisition) announced on June 9, 2026 an investment of up to ~$2.5B to build a new hot strip mill at its Mon Valley Works Edgar Thomson Plant in Braddock, Pennsylvania, replacing the ~87-year-old mill (building on an August 2024 Nippon commitment of no less than $1B for Mon Valley Works). Most recent status (as of July 2026 reporting, the freshest found): announced/planning stage, pre-construction — not yet built or in production.

Waaree Energies (Waaree Solar Americas) announced on Dec 21, 2023 a more-than-$1B, 546,000-sq-ft solar PV module manufacturing plant (3 GW/yr initial nameplate, ~1,500 direct jobs at full capacity) in Brookshire, Texas. Most recent status: the plant began commercial module production in January 2025 and is operational and expanding (April 2025: announced doubling to 3.2 GW; still producing and expanding through 2026).

Röhm (methacrylates maker owned by Advent International; with OQ Chemicals supplying feedstock) announced on June 30, 2021 a world-scale methyl methacrylate (MMA) plant (250,000 metric t/yr, the first C2-based MMA plant in North America using its LiMA technology) in Bay City, Texas; the plant is reported at ~$1.6B and clears the size floor on capital (workforce only ~70-90). Most recent status: after an Oct 27, 2022 groundbreaking, the plant completed startup/ramp-up and reached sustained full industrial-scale operation, officially opened June 8, 2026 (producing at full scale).

General Motors announced on Oct 20, 2020 a ~$2B conversion of its Spring Hill Manufacturing plant in Maury County, Tennessee to electric-vehicle production, starting with the Cadillac LYRIQ (a facility distinct from GM's Factory ZERO/Detroit-Hamtramck and Orion Assembly sites; clears the size floor on capital). Most recent status: LYRIQ production began in late 2022 and the plant now also builds the Cadillac Vistiq; as of Sept 5, 2025 GM is making strategic production cutbacks — reducing from two shifts to one for the first five months of 2026 and adding late-2025 downtime amid slower EV demand. GM's own investor release (investor.gm.com) 403s to automated clients, so the promise is cited via GM's official PR Newswire distribution of the same Oct 20, 2020 announcement.

UCB (Brussels-based biopharmaceutical company) announced on March 24, 2026 its first U.S. biologics manufacturing facility — a ~$2B, 460,000-sq-ft campus at the Rowen development in Gwinnett County, Georgia (~330 permanent jobs; clears the size floor on capital). Most recent status: as of late March 2026 reporting (and no later construction milestone found as of this Sept 2026 collection) the project is newly announced and in the planning/pre-construction phase, with production intended once the site comes online over the next several years — i.e., the 'produced' side is still early/pre-construction.

Braidy Industries announced on April 26, 2017 a ~$1.3B (later cited ~$1.6B) greenfield aluminum rolling mill (~550 direct jobs) near Ashland in Greenup County, Kentucky; clears the size floor on capital. Most recent status: the Ashland/Greenup mill was never built — it repeatedly missed financing deadlines, the company was renamed Unity Aluminum, the site was deemed too small, and by September 2022 Kentucky had recouped its controversial $15M investment while the ~200-acre site was donated back to a regional industrial authority (Unity/Steel Dynamics relocated the aluminum-mill project out of Kentucky to a separate site). The 'produced' side is therefore cancelled/never built as of Sept 2022. Both source pages return 403/429 to automated clients and were read via curl with a browser user agent per the fallback ladder; original URLs cited.

SpaceX announced 'Terafab,' a vertically integrated semiconductor fabrication plant (logic, memory and advanced packaging under one roof) at the former Gibbons Creek site in Grimes County, TX, on Aug 6, 2026, with a first phase of more than $16.8B and ~3,000 direct jobs. Most recent status available (as of Aug 2026): the county deal/tax abatement is finalized and SpaceX calls it a 'done deal' but the plant is still pre-construction, with groundbreaking expected within months.

Hanwha announced on Aug 26, 2025 a ~$5B expansion of Hanwha Philly Shipyard in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (two additional docks, three quays, and a reviewed new block-assembly facility) to raise annual output from fewer than 2 vessels to up to 20, building LNG carriers, MR oil/chemical tankers and naval modules/blocks. Single physical facility; commercial shipbuilding manufacturing. As of the most recent (2026) reporting the yard is completing MARAD training ships, a Matson containership series and MR-tanker/LNG-carrier work while the $5B buildout proceeds and Hanwha weighs a second U.S. yard. Clears the floor on capital.

Toyota announced on Apr 25, 2024 a ~$1.4B investment at its Princeton (Toyota Indiana) assembly plant in Indiana to add an all-new three-row battery-electric SUV line plus a new lithium-ion battery-pack assembly building (~340 direct jobs). Clears the floor on capital. This is a distinct site from Toyota's separate Georgetown, Kentucky EV plant. As of the most recent reporting (Apr 2026) the Princeton EV is still pre-production, now slated to begin later in 2026 (postponed from an earlier 2025 target); some three-row EV models were reallocated to the Georgetown, KY plant, but Princeton retains an all-electric SUV program.

Johnson & Johnson (Janssen Biotech) announced on Feb 18, 2026 a more-than-$1B next-generation cell-therapy manufacturing facility on a 154-acre parcel at 1201 Sumneytown Pike in Lower Gwynedd Township, Montgomery County, Pennsylvania, to make cell therapies for cancer (e.g. multiple myeloma) and other diseases (~500 permanent biomanufacturing jobs). Clears the floor on capital. Distinct site from J&J's separate ~$2B Wilson, North Carolina biologics campus. As of the most recent reporting the project is pre-construction: construction is slated to begin in the second half of 2026, with cell-therapy production expected in 2031.

DG Fuels proposed (Louisiana Economic Development announcement, March 2023) a greenfield sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) / renewable-fuel manufacturing complex on a ~3,000-acre site in St. James Parish, Louisiana, U.S. -- original announcement ~$3.1B capital and ~1,055 direct jobs (Fischer-Tropsch SAF and renewable diesel, initially ~120 million gal/yr). MOST RECENT STATUS (Nov 10, 2025): still pre-construction; scope grown to ~$8B and ~200 million gal/yr, Samsung E&A appointed contractor for the hydrogen/power scope (FEED starting late 2025), final investment decision targeted Q3 2026, commercial production expected ~2028.

Grön Fuels LLC (a Fidelis New Energy portfolio company) announced (Louisiana Economic Development, November 2020) a greenfield renewable-fuels manufacturing complex at the Port of Greater Baton Rouge (Port Allen / West Baton Rouge Parish), Louisiana, U.S. -- announced up to ~$9.2B capital over multiple phases and ~1,025 direct jobs, producing sustainable aviation fuel, renewable diesel, renewable naphtha and renewable propane. MOST RECENT STATUS FOUND is stale (~April 29, 2024): still pre-FID and awaiting finalized IRA rules, design re-phased to build the SAF portion first, operational target pushed from 2025 to 2027; no more-recent public update surfaced, so the project appears to have gone quiet/stalled since 2024.

Nacero Inc. announced (April 2021, with the Odessa Development Corporation) a greenfield natural-gas-to-gasoline (GTG) manufacturing plant in Penwell, Ector County, Texas, U.S. -- announced ~$6.5-7B capital (~115,000 bbl/day of low-carbon gasoline with carbon capture; ~350 permanent operations jobs). Clears the floor on capital. MOST RECENT STATUS (Oct 22, 2024): stalled -- Nacero canceled the plant's Clean Air Act construction permits on Oct 10, 2024, the project was described as delayed by at least six years, and it is unclear when the company will reapply for permits.

Corning Inc. (via its Solar Technology subsidiary) announced a greenfield solar ingot-and-wafer manufacturing plant in Richland Township, Michigan, U.S. on Feb 27, 2024 - originally ~$900M and ~1,100 direct jobs, then expanded in April 2025 to ~$1.5B and ~1,500 jobs. Co-located with Hemlock Semiconductor polysilicon; ingot/wafer production came online in Q3 2025, billed as the largest U.S. solar ingot/wafer facility (most recent status: Oct 2025).

HIF Global (Highly Innovative Fuels) announced on April 28, 2022 its ~$6B HIF Matagorda eFuels facility in Matagorda County (near Bay City), Texas, U.S. - a synthetic-fuels plant combining captured CO2 with green hydrogen to produce ~200M gallons/yr of carbon-neutral e-gasoline / e-methanol (~125+ permanent operating jobs; ~3,000 construction). Most recent status (Sept 16, 2025): still pre-final-investment-decision, in FEED with Bechtel/Siemens Energy/Topsoe and having selected Electric Hydrogen to supply ~1.8 GW of electrolyzers; FID was reported still pending as of mid-2025 amid U.S. clean-hydrogen tax-credit uncertainty.

Linde plc announced on Feb 15, 2023 a ~$1.8B investment to build, own and operate a clean-hydrogen and industrial-gas complex (autothermal reforming with carbon capture plus a large air-separation unit) in Beaumont, Jefferson County, Texas, U.S. It is a distinct Linde-owned facility from the co-located OCI (now Woodside) 'Beaumont New Ammonia' plant it supplies over the fence. Most recent status (late 2025): construction nearly complete; the neighboring ammonia plant reached first production in late 2025, and Linde's hydrogen plant is set to supply clean hydrogen from 2026, with CO2 offtake to ExxonMobil for permanent sequestration.

Merck announced (originally in 2021) a ~$1B, 225,000-sq-ft vaccine drug-substance manufacturing facility at its Durham, North Carolina site to expand HPV (Gardasil/Gardasil 9) production; the plant opened March 11, 2025. Most recent status (Spectrum News, Feb 27, 2026): Merck is winding down Gardasil production at the Durham site — characterized as a plant closure — and laying off 150+ workers (147 at the Old Oxford Road plant plus 7 nearby), effective by May 1, 2026, citing a ~39% worldwide drop in Gardasil demand. No update found after Feb/Mar 2026, so that is the freshest credible status as of Sep 2026.

L3Harris Technologies announced on April 15, 2026 a ~$1.27B (cited ~$1.265-1.3B) expansion of its solid rocket motor production site in Orange County, Virginia, creating the Virginia Advanced Propulsion Facilities (VAPF) - more than doubling manufacturing space (mixing, grinding, casting and final assembly for DoD solid rocket motor programs) and adding more than 350 jobs over five years. Most recent status (Manufacturing Dive, Apr 16, 2026): newly announced and in early/planning stage - no groundbreaking date disclosed as of that report, and no later construction milestone found, so as of Sep 2026 the project is not yet built. It builds on a smaller (~$41M, April 2024) modernization at the same site.

Highland Materials announced on April 23, 2024 (with a US$255.6M federal 48C tax credit) a ~$1 billion greenfield solar-grade polysilicon manufacturing plant ('Project Rocks'; 16,000 t/yr initial capacity, rising to 20,000 t/yr; ~400 permanent jobs) later sited at the former Phipps Bend nuclear site in Hawkins County (Surgoinsville), Tennessee. Most recent status (constructionreviewonline, June 1, 2026): still in engineering/pre-construction; land leased Aug 2025; on-site construction scheduled to begin Q4 2026; commercial operation targeted late 2027/early 2028. Not yet producing.

Marathon Petroleum announced in 2020 (board decision to proceed; 50/50 JV with Neste finalized 2021) a ~$1.2 billion conversion of its idled Martinez, California refinery into 'Martinez Renewable Fuels,' a renewable-diesel manufacturing plant sized to ~730 million gal/yr (~47,700 b/d) at full rate by end of 2023. Most recent status (Inside Climate News, July 23, 2026): the plant reached full capacity and continues producing renewable diesel, but a Nov 2023 fatality-injury fire and an April 2026 USW Local 5 strike that became a company lockout leave it running with an understaffed workforce amid a contract dispute.

Enterprise Products Partners announced on Sept 26, 2019 a second propane dehydrogenation plant ('PDH 2', ~$1.23 billion) at its Mont Belvieu complex in Chambers County, Texas, sized to consume ~35,000 b/d of propane and produce ~1.65 billion lb/yr of polymer-grade propylene, with in-service targeted for Q2 2023. Most recent status: PDH 2 entered service in August 2023 and is listed as an operating asset (25 MBbl/d net plant capacity) in Enterprise's FY2024 Form 10-K (as of Dec 31, 2024); the freshest dedicated reporting is the 2023 startup, with no disruption reported since.

Bayport Polymers ('Baystar', a 50/50 JV of Total/TotalEnergies and Novealis Holdings, itself a Borealis-NOVA Chemicals JV) broke ground on June 4, 2018 on a ~$1.7 billion (later cited ~$2 billion) ethane steam cracker (1 million tonnes/yr ethylene) at the TotalEnergies Port Arthur refinery in Jefferson County, Texas, originally expected to start up in 2020. Most recent status: the cracker began commercial operations in July 2022 (a ~2-year slip from the announced timeline) and supplies ethylene to Baystar's Texas polyethylene units; the freshest dedicated reporting is the July 2022 commercial startup, with the plant operating since and no disruption reported.

NXTClean Fuels (formerly NEXT Renewable Fuels) is developing a ~$2.5 billion greenfield renewable diesel and sustainable aviation fuel refinery (up to 50,000 barrels/day; ~240 permanent jobs, ~3,500 construction) at Port Westward near Clatskanie, Columbia County, Oregon, US. Most recent status (Columbia County Spotlight, Mar 31, 2026): not yet under construction — awaiting the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers' final federal permit (draft EIS in public comment through Apr 20, 2026; Corps decision anticipated summer 2026), with operations targeted for 2028–2029. Note: the promise_source (Biodiesel Magazine) 403s a default fetch client but loads with a browser user agent over HTTP/1.1.

Montana Renewables (a Calumet subsidiary) is undertaking a major sustainable-aviation-fuel/renewable-fuels expansion ('MaxSAF') at its Great Falls, Montana refinery, backed by a $1.44B ($1.67B with capitalized interest) U.S. DOE loan facility that closed Jan 10, 2025; the expansion was originally estimated at ~$1.2B to lift capacity toward ~315M gal/yr. Most recent status (BioEnergy Times, Sep 5, 2026): the company sharply cut the remaining expansion cost to ~$137M by repurposing adjacent asphalt-plant equipment, the DOE Phase 2 draw was reduced to a final $34M (from ~$658M), and SAF output (~60M gal/yr currently) is being ramped in phases toward ~80M (end 2026), ~120M (spring 2027) and ~200M gal/yr (end 2028).

USA BioEnergy announced on Feb 15, 2022 (Texas Gov. Abbott release) a $1.7B greenfield 'advanced biorefinery' at Bon Wier, Newton County, Texas, US, to convert wood waste into sustainable aviation fuel, renewable diesel and naphtha (~142 permanent jobs at announcement). The project's stated scope has since grown to ~$2.8B. Most recent status (company PR, Jan 14, 2025): USA BioEnergy closed on 1,600+ acres and the plant was 'in detailed design and engineering' (construction expected to take ~2 years once engineering completes), with ~200 permanent jobs and a 20-year Southwest Airlines SAF offtake; no more-recent public update on a construction start was found as of Sep 2026.

World Energy and Air Products announced on Apr 22, 2022 a ~$2B major expansion of World Energy's Paramount, California sustainable aviation fuel hub (a converted refinery), targeting ~340M gal/yr (a ~700% output increase) using Honeywell Ecofining technology. Most recent status of the promised expansion (Biobased Diesel, Feb 24-25, 2025): Air Products terminated the agreement and is exiting the site, so the planned expansion is cancelled (part of a pretax charge of up to $3.1B across three exited projects); World Energy said its pre-existing smaller SAF operations were unaffected at that time, though later reporting on the legacy plant's output is mixed.

Octapharma (Swiss biopharmaceutical company) announced on July 29, 2026 its first-ever U.S. manufacturing facility: a ~$1.5B plasma-derived critical-care/biologics production campus (50-acre site, ~1,500 direct jobs) at Palmetto Research Park in Rock Hill, York County, South Carolina. Most recent status (late July 2026 reporting): final state approvals secured/deal finalized; still pre-construction, with production expected to begin in the mid-2030s.

Microporous LLC announced on Nov 13, 2024 a greenfield lithium-ion battery separator manufacturing plant on Lot 1 of the Southern Virginia Megasite (Berry Hill) in Danville/Pittsylvania County, Virginia, originally ~$1.35B with 2,000+ direct jobs (later cited ~$1.6B, ~1,800 jobs). Distinct site/company from the ENTEK separator plant. Most recent status (construction start celebrated May 22, 2026, after final funding secured): now under construction in phases; plant not yet producing.

SSAB (Swedish steelmaker) was selected by the U.S. Department of Energy on Mar 25, 2024 (up to $500M award) for a first-of-its-kind commercial-scale 'green steel' hydrogen direct-reduced-iron (DRI) plant in Perry County, Mississippi, a facility SSAB valued at roughly $3.5B (~540 permanent jobs), relying on green hydrogen from Hy Stor Energy. Most recent status (Jan 2025 reporting): SSAB withdrew from the DOE award negotiations and DOE's program page lists it as no longer moving forward; the Perry County plant has effectively been scrapped/cancelled.

Slate Auto announced on Apr 30, 2025 a ~$383.5M EV pickup assembly plant, converting the former R.R. Donnelley printing plant near Warsaw (Kosciusko County), Indiana into a vertically integrated vehicle/battery-pack/seat assembly facility with 2,000+ direct jobs and up to 150,000 vehicles/yr. Clears the size floor on jobs (>2,000 direct); capital ~$0.38B is below the $1B figure. Most recent status (InkFreeNews, June 30, 2026): factory nearing production with assembly robots installed; production targeted for end of 2026 and first customer deliveries in Q4 2026 — as of this writing not yet producing.

USA Rare Earth announced on June 2, 2026 a ~$1.2B rare-earth metal and NdFeB permanent-magnet manufacturing plant (800,000 sq ft, ~490 direct jobs; targeting 6,400 t/yr sintered magnets and 5,000 t/yr strip-cast metal/alloy) in Bailey Industrial Park, Blacksburg, Cherokee County, South Carolina. Status source is the most recent update: the company broke ground on Sep 9, 2026, with commissioning targeted to begin in 2028.

Gevo broke ground in September 2022 on Net-Zero 1 (NZ1), a greenfield commercial-scale alcohol-to-jet sustainable aviation fuel plant in Lake Preston, South Dakota (designed for ~60 million gal/yr SAF plus animal feed/protein and corn oil; project cost stated at $1 billion or more, later backed by a conditional DOE loan guarantee of up to $1.46B). Status source is the most recent update: on April 15, 2026 Gevo announced it had withdrawn its DOE loan-guarantee application and is pursuing alternative financing, with the project (rebranded ATJ-30) still pre-final-investment-decision and targeting financing by the end of 2026.

Smithfield Foods announced on Feb 16, 2026 a new greenfield combined packaged-meats and fresh-pork processing facility (up to $1.3B, ~1.1M sq ft on a 211-acre Foundation Park site) in Sioux Falls, South Dakota, replacing its century-old Sioux Falls plant. As of the most recent reporting (late March 2026) the project was in city permitting/TIF approvals; site work targeted for spring 2026, groundbreaking in H1 2027, and production by end of 2028 (not yet under construction).

ExxonMobil announced on May 2, 2019 a ~$2B chemical-production expansion at its Baytown, Texas complex, adding a Vistamaxx performance-polymer unit (~400,000 t/yr) and a linear-alpha-olefins unit (~350,000 t/yr), with ~200 direct jobs and startup originally targeted for 2022. Per the most recent status reporting, both units entered service on Sept 19, 2023 (completed on budget, on schedule) and are producing.

Philip Morris International (PMI U.S.) announced on July 16, 2024 a greenfield nicotine-pouch (ZYN) manufacturing campus in Aurora, Colorado, originally framed as a ~$600M / ~500-direct-job project; PMI subsequently scaled it to a planned ~$1.2B investment (2024-2028) on a ~148-acre site. Per the most recent reporting (Axios, July 27, 2026), the Aurora campus is producing and ramping up (first products made ~September 2025; ~170 of ~500 eventual jobs filled). Note: status page 403s on default fetch; read via curl with a browser user agent.

Integra Technologies announced on Feb 2, 2023 a ~$1.8B greenfield OSAT (outsourced semiconductor assembly and test) plant and headquarters (~1M sq ft, ~2,000 direct jobs) in the Wichita/Bel Aire, Kansas area, contingent on federal CHIPS Act funding. Most recent status: the state APEX incentive package expired in Oct 2024 for lack of federal funding, Micross Components acquired Integra in Jan 2025, and construction had not started; per reporting through early 2025 (Wikipedia current to mid-2026) the project remains in a holding pattern pending CHIPS funding. No update newer than early 2025 was found.

MP Materials announced on Feb 26, 2026 a >$1.25B greenfield rare-earth NdFeB permanent-magnet manufacturing campus ('10X', 120 acres, ~1,500 direct jobs) in Northlake, Denton County, Texas - a new facility distinct from its existing Fort Worth 'Independence' magnet plant. Most recent status (MP Q2 2026 earnings, Aug 13, 2026): site purchased (~$80M in Q2), construction accelerating with engineering/equipment underway; commissioning targeted for 2028. Sector: other (rare-earth magnet manufacturing).

GSK announced on Sep 17, 2025 a ~$1.2B new AI-driven biologics 'flex' factory at its existing Upper Merion (King of Prussia) campus in Montgomery County, Pennsylvania, to make biologics for respiratory disease (COPD/asthma) and cancer; 'hundreds' of direct jobs (facility clears the floor on capital, not jobs). Most recent status available (as of 2026) is still early/pre-construction: the project remained in the planning phase with construction expected to begin in 2026 - no groundbreaking reported yet. Sector: pharmaceuticals (biologics).

Ford announced on Aug 11, 2025 a ~$2B conversion of its Louisville Assembly Plant in Louisville, Kentucky, retooling the 70-year-old plant (former Ford Escape / Lincoln Corsair site) to build a new sub-$30,000 midsize electric pickup ('Fathom') on Ford's new Universal EV Production System; ~2,200 hourly jobs secured (facility clears the floor on capital). Most recent status (Detroit News, Aug 13, 2026): retooling largely completed within about a year, with equipment installation and quality verification continuing through end of 2026 and prototype/production launch targeted for early 2027. Sector: auto assembly.

Hanwha Defense USA (a subsidiary of South Korea's Hanwha Group) was awarded an enhanced-use lease by the U.S. Army on Jan 28, 2026 to build a ~$1.3B munitions/energetic-materials manufacturing campus (~1,065 acres, ~200 direct jobs) at Pine Bluff Arsenal, Arkansas, producing components for explosives and propellants (e.g., for 155mm artillery). Distinct from Hanwha's Philly Shipyard. Most recent status (Deltaplex News, Sep 3, 2026): still in the enhanced-use-lease/development phase, ~1,065 acres and ~$1.3B reaffirmed; no groundbreaking or construction reported yet.

Encina Development Group announced on April 21, 2022 a ~$1.1 billion 'Point Township Circular Manufacturing Facility' (advanced/chemical recycling of post-consumer plastics into BTX aromatic feedstock; ~300 direct full-time jobs) in Point Township, Northumberland County, Pennsylvania. Most recent status: Encina withdrew the project in April 2024 (notifying PA DEP of intent to withdraw); as of the latest reporting the facility is cancelled and will not be built.
